title: Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves, Part II: Gabber's finiteness, affine Lefschetz and duality theorems on quasi-excellent schemes
summary: This Part II extends Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves beyond schemes of finite type over a field or a one-dimensional base. Following Gabber's work as written in Illusie–Laszlo–Orgogozo, it plans the topology of ℓ′-alterations, the Cohen–Gabber theorem and partial algebraization, Gabber's weak and prime-to-ℓ local uniformization, oriented products and oriented cohomological descent, Gabber's finiteness theorem for quasi-excellent schemes, dimension functions, the affine Lefschetz theorem and the cohomological dimension bound, and dualizing complexes on excellent schemes with Gabber's duality theorem and local duality. It ends with the local results of Česnavičius–Scholze: local absolute purity, the Lefschetz hyperplane theorem in local étale cohomology, and the algebraic tilting of étale cohomology of henselian perfectoid pairs.
readme: This roadmap starts where Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves) stops: that roadmap works with separated schemes of finite type over a field or an excellent regular base of dimension at most one and leaves general absolute purity and quasi-excellent bases to extensions. Absolute cohomological purity itself is LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §0.10 and is imported. The layers EQ.0–EQ.6 plan the étale cohomology of noetherian quasi-excellent schemes after Gabber (finiteness, affine Lefschetz, duality), EQ.7 the local consequences used by PurityForFlatCohomology, and EQ.8 the algebraic tilting of étale cohomology of Česnavičius–Scholze. The full document is research/blueprint/readmes/EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheavesPartII.md.

stages.title: Topologies of alterations and approximation
stages.description:
## EQ.0. Topologies of alterations and approximation

The topologies in which Gabber's uniformization is stated, and the two reductions of uniformization to complete local rings.

Targets:

- The category alt/S of maximally finite dominant schemes (`alteration-category`): Let S be a noetherian scheme and ℓ a prime, the integer 1 or the symbol ∞ (with ℓ′ the set of positive integers prime to ℓ, and ∞′ = {1}). A morphism f : X → Y is maximally dominant if it sends every maximal point (generic point of an irreducible component) of X to a maximal point of Y; it is maximally ℓ′-finite if for every maximal point η of X the extension κ(η)/κ(f(η)) is finite and every maximal point μ of Y in the image of f has a maximal point η above it with [κ(η) : κ(μ)] ∈ ℓ′ (maximally finite when ℓ = 1, where the second condition is empty). alt/S is the category whose objects are reduced S-schemes of finite type whose structure map is maximally finite and maximally dominant, with S-morphisms as morphisms. For X of finite type over S, X^md is the closure of the image of the generic fibre X ×_S η_S with its reduced structure (the union of the irreducible components of X dominating a component of S). Fibre products in alt/S are X ×^alt_S Y := (X ×_S Y)^md.
- The topology of ℓ′-alterations (`ell-prime-alteration-topology`): Let S be noetherian and ℓ as in EQ.0/alteration-category. An étale covering (X_i → X) is ℓ′-decomposed if every point x of X lifts to a point x_i of some X_i with [κ(x_i) : κ(x)] ∈ ℓ′ (for ℓ = 1 an ordinary étale covering, for ℓ = ∞ a Nisnevich covering). The topology alt_ℓ′ of ℓ′-alterations on alt/S is the Grothendieck topology generated by (i) ℓ′-decomposed étale coverings and (ii) single morphisms that are proper, surjective and maximally ℓ′-finite. alt_1′ is the alteration topology alt. A hypercovering for alt_ℓ′ of X is a simplicial object X_• of alt/X with X_0 → X an alt_ℓ′-covering and whose maps X_{n+1} → (cosk_n X_•)_{n+1} are alt_ℓ′-coverings.
- Standard forms of alteration coverings (`standard-form-covers`): Let X be irreducible, noetherian and quasi-excellent, and ℓ a prime. (1) Every alt_ℓ′-covering family of X is refined by a family (V_i → Y → X)_i in which Y is integral, Y → X is proper, surjective, of generic degree prime to ℓ, and (V_i → Y)_i is a Nisnevich covering; for ℓ = 1 one may take (V_i → Y) a Zariski covering. (2) Every alt_ℓ′-covering family of X is refined by a family (W_i → V_i → Y → X)_i of irreducible schemes in which Y → X is a proper birational modification, (V_i → Y) is a Nisnevich covering and each W_i → V_i is finite, flat and of degree prime to ℓ. For reducible X apply (2) to the disjoint union of the irreducible components.
- Valuative characterisation of alteration coverings (`valuative-alteration-covers`): Let X be noetherian and Y → X an object of alt/X. Then Y → X is a covering for the alteration topology if and only if every maximally dominant morphism Spec V → X, with V a valuation ring whose fraction field is algebraically closed, lifts to a morphism Spec V → Y. The analogue for alt_ℓ′ replaces the algebraically closed fraction field by a perfect field whose absolute Galois group is a pro-ℓ group (the quotient of the geometric generic point by an ℓ-Sylow subgroup).
- Approximation of schemes over a complete local ring (`artin-popescu-approximation`): Let A be an excellent henselian noetherian local ring with completion Â, S = Spec A, Ŝ = Spec Â, and write Ŝ = lim_α S_α with S_α smooth over S (Popescu). Let X be of finite type over Ŝ with a model X_{α0} over S_{α0}. There are α1 ≥ α0 and integers n0 ≥ c > 0 such that for every n ≥ n0, α ≥ α1 and every section u of S_α → S that is (n+1)-close to the canonical map Ŝ → S_α, the pulled-back scheme X_u over S is (n+1−c)-isomorphic to X above the closed fibre (an approximation of order n − c). If X and Y are a-close at a point x of their common closed fibre, then (i) for a ≥ 1 they have the same dimension at x, and (ii) for a ≥ 2, X is regular at x iff Y is; (iii) if X is regular, every sufficiently fine approximation X_u is regular in an open neighbourhood of its closed fibre.
- Reduction of uniformization to local henselian excellent normal schemes (`uniformization-henselian-reduction`): Consider the uniformization statement U(X): for every nowhere dense closed Z ⊂ X there is a finite family (X_i → X) covering for alt (resp. alt_ℓ′, ℓ invertible on X) with each X_i regular and connected and each preimage of Z the support of a strict normal crossings divisor (possibly empty). If U(X) holds for every noetherian local henselian excellent normal scheme X (resp. of dimension ≤ d), then U(X) holds for every noetherian quasi-excellent scheme X (resp. of dimension ≤ d).
- Reduction of uniformization to complete local rings (`complete-local-reduction`): If the uniformization statement U(T) of EQ.0/uniformization-henselian-reduction (for alt, resp. alt_ℓ′ with ℓ invertible) holds for every noetherian complete local scheme T, then it holds for every noetherian quasi-excellent scheme T.

stages.title: Cohen–Gabber structure and partial algebraization
stages.description:
## EQ.1. Cohen–Gabber structure and partial algebraization

Gabber's refinement of Cohen's structure theorem (finite generically étale power-series parametrisations, equivariant and prime-to-ℓ forms, with Epp's theorem) and the partial algebraization of complete local rings as completions of finite-type schemes over regular bases of smaller dimension.

Targets:

- The Cohen–Gabber theorem in characteristic p (`cohen-gabber-equal-characteristic`): Let A be a complete noetherian local ring of equal characteristic p > 0 that is reduced and equidimensional of dimension d, with residue field k. There is a subring A_0 ⊆ A isomorphic to k⟦t_1, …, t_d⟧ such that A is finite and torsion-free over A_0 and generically étale over it (étale over a dense open of Spec A_0), and A_0 → A induces an isomorphism on residue fields.
- Equivariant Cohen–Gabber theorem (`cohen-gabber-equivariant`): Let A be a complete noetherian local reduced ring of equal characteristic, of dimension d, with residue field κ, and let a finite group G act on A with |G| invertible in κ. There is a G-equivariant finite generically étale morphism κ⟦t_1, …, t_d⟧ → A, where κ → A lifts the identity of κ and G acts trivially on the t_i. Here generic étaleness means étaleness over a dense open of the power-series target; lower-dimensional components of Spec A can disappear over that open.
- Epp's theorem on eliminating wild ramification (`epp-theorem`): Let T → S be a local dominant morphism of complete traits of residue characteristic p > 0, with residue fields κ_S perfect and the maximal perfect subfield of κ_T algebraic over κ_S. There is a finite extension of traits S′ → S such that the normalisation of the reduced fibre product, T′ = ((T ×_S S′)_red)^norm, has reduced special fibre over S′. In mixed characteristic T ×_S S′ is already reduced.
- The Cohen–Gabber theorem in mixed characteristic, prime to ℓ (`cohen-gabber-mixed-characteristic`): Let X = Spec A be a complete noetherian local normal scheme of dimension d ≥ 2 with residue field k of characteristic p > 0 and generic point of characteristic 0. (1) There are a finite surjective X′ → X with X′ normal integral of residue field k′, and a finite surjective X′ → Spec V⟦t_1, …, t_{d−1}⟧ with V a discrete valuation ring of residue field k′, étale over a p-dense open (an open meeting the fibre over p densely). (2) For a prime ℓ ≠ p there are a normal integral local Y with an action of a finite ℓ-group H and an H-equivariant finite surjective Y → X with Y/H → X of generic degree prime to ℓ, a complete mixed-characteristic discrete valuation ring V with residue field that of Y and a compatible H-action, and an H-equivariant local finite morphism Y → Spec V⟦t_1, …, t_{d−1}⟧, étale over a p-dense open, with H acting trivially on the t_i.
- Partially algebraizable complete local rings (`partially-algebraizable`): Let A be a complete noetherian local ring and (I_e)_{e∈E} a family of ideals of A. The pair (A, (I_e)) is partially algebraizable if there exist a complete noetherian local ring B with dim B < dim A, a B-algebra C of finite type, a maximal ideal 𝔫 of C above the maximal ideal of B, and an isomorphism A ≅ Ĉ_𝔫 (completion of the localisation) under which every I_e is the extension of an ideal of C_𝔫.
- Partial algebraization in equal characteristic (`partial-algebraization-equal-characteristic`): Let A be a complete noetherian local reduced ring of equal characteristic which is not a field. Then for every finite family of ideals (I_e), the pair (A, (I_e)) is partially algebraizable.
- Partial algebraization prime to ℓ in mixed characteristic (`partial-algebraization-mixed-characteristic`): Let A be a complete noetherian local normal ring of mixed characteristic (0, p) and dimension d ≥ 2, and ℓ ≠ p a prime. There is a finite injective A → A′ of generic degree prime to ℓ with A′ normal integral such that every finite family of ideals of A′ is partially algebraizable. Geometrically: for a complete noetherian local normal X of mixed characteristic and dimension d ≥ 2, finitely many closed subsets Z_i ⊂ X and ℓ invertible on X, there are a complete regular local scheme S of mixed characteristic and dimension d − 1, a local normal X′ with a finite π : X′ → X of generic degree prime to ℓ, a finite-type f : Y → S and an isomorphism a of X′ with the completion of Y at a closed point of its special fibre, and closed F_i ⊂ Y with π^{-1}(Z_i) = a^{-1}(F_i). For X reduced of equal characteristic and not a field, the analogous presentation over a complete regular local base of dimension dim X − 1 holds with X′ = X (V 3.1.4).

stages.title: Gabber's local uniformization
stages.description:
## EQ.2. Gabber's local uniformization

de Jong's equivariant nodal-curve alteration over excellent bases, Gabber's weak and prime-to-ℓ local uniformization theorems for noetherian quasi-excellent schemes, and alteration hypercoverings by regular schemes with snc boundary.

Targets:

- de Jong's equivariant nodal-curve alteration over an excellent base (`de-jong-nodal-curve-alteration`): Let f : X → Y be a proper morphism of excellent integral noetherian schemes and Z ⊂ X a nowhere dense closed subscheme, with η the generic point of Y, such that X_η is smooth, geometrically irreducible and of dimension 1 and Z_η is étale over η. There are a finite group G, a commutative square of G-schemes with f′ : X′ → Y′ over f, alterations a : X′ → X and b : Y′ → Y, an effective G-equivariant divisor D ⊂ X′ and a nowhere dense G-stable closed T′ ⊂ Y′ such that: f′ is projective; G acts trivially on X and Y and freely on Y′ − T′; a and b are projective generically étale alterations and Y′/G → Y (resp. X′/G → X) is an isomorphism at η (resp. at the generic point of X_η); f′ is a nodal curve, smooth outside T′; D is étale over Y′ and contained in the smooth locus of f′; and a^{-1}(Z) ⊂ D ∪ f′^{-1}(T′).
- Gabber's weak local uniformization theorem (`weak-local-uniformization`): Let X be a noetherian quasi-excellent scheme and Z ⊂ X a nowhere dense closed subset. There is a finite family (X_i → X)_{i∈I}, covering for the alteration topology alt, such that each X_i is regular and connected and the preimage of Z in X_i is the support of a strict normal crossings divisor (possibly empty).
- Gabber's prime-to-ℓ local uniformization theorem (`prime-to-ell-local-uniformization`): Let X be a noetherian quasi-excellent scheme, Z ⊂ X a nowhere dense closed subset and ℓ a prime invertible on X. There is a finite family (p_i : X_i → X)_{i∈I}, covering for the topology alt_ℓ′ of ℓ′-alterations, such that each X_i is regular and connected and p_i^{-1}(Z) is the support of a strict normal crossings divisor.
- Hypercoverings by regular schemes with snc boundary (`regular-alteration-hypercover`): Let X be a noetherian quasi-excellent scheme, Z ⊂ X a closed subset with dense complement U, and N ≥ 0. There is a hypercovering ε : X_• → X for the alteration topology (resp. for alt_ℓ′ with ℓ invertible on X) such that for every i ≤ N the scheme X_i is regular (a finite disjoint union of regular connected schemes) and the preimage of Z in X_i is the support of a strict normal crossings divisor, so that U_i = U ×_X X_i is the complement of an snc divisor. The X_i may be chosen affine.

stages.title: Oriented products and oriented cohomological descent
stages.description:
## EQ.3. Oriented products and oriented cohomological descent

Deligne's oriented product of topoi for general bases, base change for tubes, the oriented alteration topology, oriented proper acyclicity, oriented cohomological descent and the base change formula along alteration hypercoverings.

Targets:

- Deligne's oriented product of topoi (`oriented-product-topos`): Let f : X → S and g : Y → S be morphisms of topoi, with defining sites C_1, C_2, D having finite limits and f^*, g^* induced by continuous finite-limit-preserving functors. The oriented product X ←×_S Y is the topos of sheaves on the site C whose objects are triples (U → V ← W) with V ∈ D, U ∈ C_1, W ∈ C_2 and maps U → f^*V, g^*V ← W, with the topology generated by (a) coverings in the U variable, (b) coverings in the W variable, and (c) the maps (U → V′ ← W ×_V V′) → (U → V ← W) for V′ → V in D such that U → f^*V factors through f^*V′. It carries projections p_1 : X ←×_S Y → X, p_2 : X ←×_S Y → Y and a canonical 2-morphism τ : g p_2 ⇒ f p_1. For schemes it is applied to the étale topoi; for S a henselian trait, X_s ←×_S η is LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0's oriented product.
- Base change for tubes of oriented products (`tube-base-change`): Let f : X → S and g : Y → S be coherent morphisms of coherent topoi, T = X ←×_S Y with projections p_1, p_2 and τ : g p_2 ⇒ f p_1, and Λ a ring. For every F ∈ D⁺(Y, Λ) the base change map f^*Rg_*F → Rp_{1*}p_2^*F deduced from τ is an isomorphism in D⁺(X, Λ).
- The oriented alteration topology on diagrams X → S ← Y (`oriented-alteration-topology`): Fix a noetherian base S₀. Let B be the category of diagrams (X → S ← Y) of finite-type S₀-schemes, with morphisms the commutative S₀-ladders; finite limits and finite coproducts in B are computed termwise. The oriented alteration topology on B is generated by the families: (i) (X → S ← Y_i) → (X → S ← Y) for an alteration covering (Y_i → Y); (ii) (X_i → S ← Y) → (X → S ← Y) for an alteration covering (X_i → X); (iii) (X ×_S S_i → S_i ← Y ×_S S_i) → (X → S ← Y) for an alteration covering (S_i → S); (iv) (X → S′ ← Y ×_S S′) → (X → S ← Y) for S′ → S proper through which X → S factors; (v) (X ×_S S′ → S′ ← Y) → (X → S ← Y) for S′ → S étale through which Y → S factors (ILO XII 2.1.1–2.1.2). An oriented alteration hypercovering of (X → S ← Y) is a simplicial object (X_• → S_• ← Y_•) of B whose degree-zero augmentation and all positive-degree matching maps are coverings for this topology; its augmentation induces ←ε : Y_• ←×_{S_•} X_• → Y ←×_S X.
- Oriented acyclicity of proper morphisms (`oriented-proper-acyclicity`): Let S be a coherent scheme, g : Y → S, π : S′ → S proper, a : X → S′ coherent, b = π a, Y′ = Y ×_S S′ with g′ : Y′ → S′ and ρ : Y′ → Y. The induced morphism ←ρ : Y′ ←×_{S′} X → Y ←×_S X of oriented products is acyclic for torsion sheaves: for every torsion abelian sheaf (more generally bounded below torsion complex) F on Y ←×_S X, F → R←ρ_* ←ρ^* F is an isomorphism. The companion assertion of 1-acyclicity for ind-finite stacks is recorded with proof gap NONABELIAN-ORIENTED-LIMIT; the abelian theorem does not depend on it.
- Oriented cohomological descent (`oriented-cohomological-descent`): Let (X_• → S_• ← Y_•) → (X → S ← Y) be a hypercovering for the oriented alteration topology, with augmentation ←ε : T_• = Y_• ←×_{S_•} X_• → T = Y ←×_S X. For every bounded below torsion complex K on T, the adjunction K → R←ε_* ←ε^* K is an isomorphism; the companion descent assertion for ind-finite stacks C, namely C → ←ε_* ←ε^* C, requires the limit input recorded in gap NONABELIAN-ORIENTED-LIMIT.
- Base change formula for alteration hypercoverings (`alteration-hypercover-base-change`): Let X —f→ S ←g— Y be finite-type morphisms of noetherian schemes and ε : S_• → S an alteration hypercovering, with f_• : X_• = X ×_S S_• → S_•, g_• : Y_• = Y ×_S S_• → S_• and ε_Y : Y_• → Y. For every bounded below torsion complex K on X, the natural map g^*Rf_*K → Rε_{Y*}(g_•^*Rf_{•*}(K|X_•)) is an isomorphism. The corresponding ind-finite-stack assertion g^*f_*C → ε_{Y*}(g_•^*f_{•*}(C|X_•)) remains conditional on gap NONABELIAN-ORIENTED-LIMIT.

stages.title: Gabber's finiteness theorem
stages.description:
## EQ.4. Gabber's finiteness theorem

Constructibility and boundedness of higher direct images along finite-type morphisms to noetherian quasi-excellent schemes, with coefficients invertible on the base.

Targets:

- Constructibility of direct images via weak uniformization (`constructibility-via-weak-uniformization`): Let X be a noetherian quasi-excellent scheme, f : Y → X a morphism of finite type, n ≥ 1 invertible on X and F a constructible sheaf of ℤ/n-modules on Y. Then every R^q f_*F is constructible.
- Gabber's finiteness theorem (`gabber-finiteness-theorem`): Let X be a noetherian quasi-excellent scheme, f : Y → X a morphism of finite type, n ≥ 1 invertible on X and F a constructible sheaf of ℤ/n-modules on Y. Then (i) every R^q f_*F is constructible, and (ii) there is an integer N with R^q f_*F = 0 for q ≥ N. Equivalently Rf_* : D⁺(Y_ét, ℤ/n) → D⁺(X_ét, ℤ/n) carries D^b_c(Y_ét, ℤ/n) into D^b_c(X_ét, ℤ/n).

stages.title: Dimension functions, the affine Lefschetz theorem and cohomological dimension
stages.description:
## EQ.5. Dimension functions, the affine Lefschetz theorem and cohomological dimension

Gabber's dimension functions with their existence and induced versions, regular base change, Gabber's affine Lefschetz theorem over a trait and over quasi-excellent bases, its local form, and Gabber's bound 2d − 1 on the cohomological dimension of opens of strictly local schemes.

Targets:

- Dimension functions (`dimension-function`): Let X be a locally noetherian scheme. For points x, y of X with geometric points x̄, ȳ, a specialization x̄ ⇝ ȳ is an X-morphism X_(x̄) → X_(ȳ) of strict henselizations (equivalently an X-morphism x̄ → X_(ȳ)); it has codimension r if the closure in X_(ȳ) of the image of x̄ has dimension r. y is an étale immediate specialization of x if some x̄ ⇝ ȳ has codimension 1. A dimension function on X is a map δ : X → ℤ such that δ(y) = δ(x) − 1 whenever y is an étale immediate specialization of x. For a sheaf G on X, δ(G) = sup{δ(x) : G_x̄ ≠ 0} (−∞ for G = 0).
- Existence of dimension functions (`dimension-function-existence`): (1) (Gabber) A noetherian scheme is universally catenary if and only if it admits a dimension function Zariski-locally. (2) (Gabber) Every quasi-excellent scheme admits dimension functions étale-locally, and they form an étale torsor under the sheaf of locally constant ℤ-valued functions. (3) On a normal quasi-excellent scheme, x ↦ −dim O_{X,x} is a dimension function.
- Dimension functions induced along finite-type and regular morphisms (`induced-dimension-function`): Let δ_X be a dimension function on a noetherian scheme X. (1) For f : Y → X of finite type, δ_Y(y) = δ_X(f(y)) + trdeg(κ(y)/κ(f(y))) is a dimension function on Y (written f^*δ_X). (2) For f : Y → X a regular morphism of excellent schemes, δ_Y(y) = δ_X(f(y)) − dim O_{Y_{f(y)}, y} is a dimension function on Y.
- Base change along regular morphisms (`regular-base-change`): Consider a cartesian square T′ = T ×_S S′ with f : T → S quasi-compact and quasi-separated, g : S′ → S a regular morphism of noetherian schemes, f′ : T′ → S′ and g′ : T′ → T. For n invertible on S and every sheaf F of ℤ/n-modules on T, the base change map g^*Rf_*F → Rf′_*g′^*F is an isomorphism.
- Gabber's affine Lefschetz theorem over a trait (`gabber-trait-affine-lefschetz`): Let S be a trait with the dimension function δ_S(η) = 1, δ_S(s) = 0, X a scheme of finite type over S with the induced dimension function δ_X (EQ.5/induced-dimension-function), f : Y → X an affine morphism of finite type and n invertible on S. For every constructible sheaf F of ℤ/n-modules on Y and every q, δ_X(R^q f_*F) ≤ f^*δ_X(F) − q. In particular, for a strictly local scheme X′ essentially of finite type over S of dimension d and an affine open U ⊂ X′, H^q(U, ℤ/n) = 0 for q > d.
- Gabber's affine Lefschetz theorem (`affine-lefschetz-theorem`): Let X be a quasi-excellent scheme with a dimension function δ_X, f : Y → X an affine morphism of finite type and n invertible on X. For every constructible sheaf F of ℤ/n-modules on Y and every q, δ_X(R^q f_*F) ≤ f^*δ_X(F) − q, where f^*δ_X is the induced dimension function of EQ.5/induced-dimension-function. Equivalently, for X strictly local quasi-excellent with δ_X(t) = dim of the closure of t, H^q(Y, F) = 0 for q > f^*δ_X(F).
- Local form of the affine Lefschetz theorem (`affine-lefschetz-local`): Let X be a strictly local quasi-excellent scheme of dimension d, U ⊂ X an affine open and n invertible on X. Then H^q(U, ℤ/n) = 0 for q > d. More generally, for X henselian local quasi-excellent of dimension d with residue field k and ℓ invertible on X, cd_ℓ(U) ≤ d + cd_ℓ(k) for every affine open U; if X is integral with fraction field K, cd_ℓ(K) = d + cd_ℓ(k).
- Gabber's bound on cohomological dimension (`gabber-cohomological-dimension-bound`): Let X be a strictly local noetherian scheme of dimension d > 0 and ℓ a prime invertible on X. For every open U ⊂ X, cd_ℓ(U) ≤ 2d − 1. Consequently, if X is integral with fraction field K then cd_ℓ(K) ≤ 2d − 1; and for f : X′ → Y of finite type with Y noetherian of finite dimension, Rf_* has finite ℓ-cohomological dimension.

stages.title: Dualizing complexes on excellent schemes and local duality
stages.description:
## EQ.6. Dualizing complexes on excellent schemes and local duality

Transition morphisms of local cohomology, potential dualizing complexes, Gabber's perverse t-structures, existence, uniqueness and functoriality of potential dualizing complexes, biduality, Gabber's duality theorem, the normalised dualizing complex of a regular local ring, and local duality.

Targets:

- Transition morphisms for specializations (`transition-morphism`): Let n ≥ 2, Λ = ℤ/n and X be noetherian excellent over ℤ[1/n]. For K ∈ D⁺(X_ét,Λ), write RΓ_x̄(K) for cohomology on X_(x̄) with supports in its closed point. A specialization ȳ ⇝ x̄ of codimension c = 0 or 1 gives a natural map sp : RΓ_ȳ(K) → RΓ_x̄(K)(c)[2c] in D⁺(Λ). For c = 0 it is transport along the corresponding geometric-point isomorphism. On a strictly henselian trait, first project the generic stalk to its wild-inertia invariants K_η̄^S (averaging is available for the invertible torsion coefficients); the tame-inertia evaluation construction then gives the codimension-one map independently of the generator. For an integral one-dimensional strict localization, use its normalization and multiply the trait map by 1/[s̃:s], the inverse purely inseparable residue degree. Closed-support adjunction gives the map for every immediate specialization. Higher-codimension transitions will be constructed on cohomology groups in EQ.6/top-degree-local-class; no derived map in arbitrary codimension is asserted.
- Higher transitions and top-degree local cohomology (`top-degree-local-class`): Let X be a normal strictly henselian excellent local ℤ[1/n]-scheme of dimension d with closed point x. Then H^q_x(X, Λ(d)) = 0 for q > 2d, and there is an isomorphism [x] : Λ → H^{2d}_x(X, Λ(d)) compatible with the transition morphisms of immediate specializations. Jointly, for every noetherian excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme, K ∈ D⁺(X_ét,Λ) and specialization ȳ ⇝ x̄ of codimension c, there are natural group maps sp : H^i_ȳ(K) → H^{i+2c}_x̄(K(c)), extending the codimension-zero and codimension-one derived transitions. They compose along specializations and commute with finite trace. These are maps of cohomology groups; the theorem makes no arbitrary-codimension derived-map assertion.
- Putative and potential dualizing complexes (`potential-dualizing-complex`): Let X be a noetherian excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme with a dimension function δ. A putative dualizing complex is K ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ) together with, for every x ∈ X, an isomorphism (pinning) RΓ_x(K) ≅ Λ(δ(x))[2δ(x)] in D⁺(x_ét, Λ). It is a potential dualizing complex if for every immediate specialization ȳ → x̄ the pinnings at y and x are compatible with sp_{ȳ→x̄} : RΓ_ȳ(K) → RΓ_x̄(K)(1)[2] (EQ.6/transition-morphism), using δ(y) = δ(x) + 1.
- The constant sheaf on a regular scheme is potentially dualizing (`regular-potential-dualizing`): Let X be a regular excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme with the dimension function δ = −codim. The constant sheaf Λ, with the pinnings RΓ_x(Λ) ≅ Λ(−c)[−2c] (c = codim x) given by absolute cohomological purity and the fundamental classes, is a potential dualizing complex.
- Gabber's perverse t-structures for a perversity function (`gabber-perverse-t-structure`): Let X be a noetherian scheme and p : X → ℤ ∪ {+∞} a perversity function: p(x) ≥ p(y) for every specialization ȳ → x̄ of geometric points. The pair (D^{≤p}, D^{≥p}) with K ∈ D^{≤p}(X_ét, Λ) iff K|_x ∈ D^{≤p(x)}(x_ét, Λ) for all x, and K ∈ D^{≥p} iff RΓ_x(K) ∈ D^{≥p(x)}(x_ét, Λ) for all x, is a t-structure on D⁺(X_ét, Λ). Its heart Perv^p(X, Λ) is a stack for the étale topology: objects and morphisms glue.
- Existence and uniqueness of potential dualizing complexes (`potential-dualizing-existence`): Let X be an excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme with a dimension function δ. Then (X, δ) admits a potential dualizing complex K_X, unique up to unique isomorphism preserving all pinnings, the canonical map Λ → τ_{≤0}RHom(K_X, K_X) is an isomorphism, and K_X ∈ Perv^{−2δ}(X, Λ).
- Functoriality of potential dualizing complexes (`potential-dualizing-functoriality`): Let X be a noetherian excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme with a dimension function δ_X and K a putative (resp. potential) dualizing complex. (1) For f : Y → X a regular morphism of excellent schemes and δ_Y(y) = δ_X(f(y)) − codim_{f^{-1}(f(y))}(y), f^*K is naturally putative (resp. potential) on (Y, δ_Y). (2) For f : Y → X of finite type and compactifiable and δ_Y(y) = δ_X(f(y)) + trdeg(κ(y)/κ(f(y))), f^!K is naturally putative (resp. potential) on (Y, δ_Y). Both constructions are compatible with composition.
- Dualizing complexes on noetherian schemes (`dualizing-complex`): Let X be a noetherian ℤ[1/n]-scheme and Λ = ℤ/n. A dualizing complex on X is an object K ∈ D^b_c(X_ét, Λ) such that the duality functor D_K = RHom(−, K) preserves D^b_c(X_ét, Λ) and, for every L ∈ D^b_c(X_ét, Λ), the biduality morphism L → D_K D_K L is an isomorphism. (Unlike SGA 5 I 1.7, finite quasi-injective dimension is not required.)
- Biduality for potential dualizing complexes (`gabber-biduality-theorem`): Let X be a noetherian excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme with a dimension function δ and K the potential dualizing complex of (X, δ). Then K ∈ D^b_ctf(X_ét, Λ); K has finite quasi-injective dimension iff X has finite Krull dimension; D_K = RHom(−, K) preserves D^b_c(X_ét, Λ); and for every M ∈ D^b_c(X_ét, Λ) the biduality morphism M → D_K D_K M is an isomorphism. Thus K is a dualizing complex.
- Gabber's duality theorem on excellent schemes (`gabber-duality-theorem`): Let X be a noetherian excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme admitting a dimension function. Then X has a dualizing complex K, unique up to tensoring with an invertible object; K ∈ D^b_ctf(X_ét, Λ), and K has finite quasi-injective dimension iff X has finite Krull dimension. Moreover: if X is regular, Λ is a dualizing complex; if f : Y → X is flat with geometrically regular fibres and Y noetherian excellent, f^*K is dualizing; if f : Y → X is of finite type and compactifiable, f^!K is dualizing.
- The normalised dualizing complex of a regular local ring (`regular-local-dualizing-complex`): Let R be a strictly henselian excellent regular local ring of dimension d with closed point x, ℓ a prime invertible in R, Λ = ℤ/ℓ, and δ(t) = dim of the closure of t. Then K = (μ_ℓ^{⊗d})[2d] = Λ(d)[2d] is the potential dualizing complex of (Spec R, δ), pinned at x by RΓ_x(K) ≅ Λ through absolute purity; for every open immersion j : U → Spec R, j^!K = K|_U is dualizing on U, and Rj_* ∘ D_U ≅ D_X ∘ j_! on constructible complexes.
- Local duality on strictly local excellent schemes (`local-duality`): Let X be a strictly local noetherian excellent ℤ[1/n]-scheme with closed point x, and K a dualizing complex on X pinned at x by RΓ_x(K) ≅ Λ (the potential dualizing complex for δ with δ(x) = 0). For every F ∈ D^b_c(X_ét, Λ) and every i there is a natural isomorphism H^i_x(X, F) ≅ Hom_Λ(H^{−i}(D_K F)_x̄, Λ).

stages.title: Local purity and the local Lefschetz theorem
stages.description:
## EQ.7. Local purity and the local Lefschetz theorem

Česnavičius–Scholze's local consequences: local absolute purity for finite étale coefficients and its sheafified form (from absolute purity), vanishing for principal punctured opens, and the Lefschetz hyperplane theorem in local étale cohomology.

Targets:

- Local absolute purity for finite étale coefficients (`local-absolute-purity`): Let (R, 𝔪) be a regular local ring and G a commutative finite étale R-group scheme whose order is invertible in R. Then H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < 2 dim R.
- Sheafified local purity with the cycle class (`sheafified-local-purity`): Let R be a regular local ring of dimension d and n invertible in R. The étale sheafifications ℋ^i_𝔪(−, ℤ/n) of local cohomology at the closed point vanish for i ≠ 2d, and the cycle class map ℤ/n(−d) → ℋ^{2d}_𝔪(−, ℤ/n) is an isomorphism.
- Vanishing for principal punctured opens (`punctured-affine-vanishing`): Let R be a strictly henselian excellent regular local ring of dimension d, f ∈ 𝔪 and ℓ a prime invertible in R. Then H^i(Spec R[1/f], ℤ/ℓ) = 0 for i > d.
- Local cohomology of extension by zero from a principal open (`extension-by-zero-local-vanishing`): Let R be a regular local ring of dimension d, f ∈ 𝔪, ℓ a prime invertible in R and j : Spec R[1/f] → Spec R. Then H^i_𝔪(R, j_!ℤ/ℓ) = 0 for i < d.
- Lefschetz hyperplane theorem in local étale cohomology (`local-lefschetz-hyperplane-theorem`): Let (R, 𝔪) be a regular local ring, f ∈ 𝔪 and ℓ a prime invertible in R. The restriction map H^i_𝔪(R, ℤ/ℓ) → H^i_𝔪(R/(f), ℤ/ℓ) is bijective for i < dim R − 1 and injective for i = dim R − 1.

stages.title: Tilting étale cohomology of henselian perfectoid pairs
stages.description:
## EQ.8. Tilting étale cohomology of henselian perfectoid pairs

Česnavičius–Scholze's algebraic tilting: matched punctured opens of a henselian perfectoid pair and of its tilt, the multiplicative tilt of the generic fibre, tilting of idempotents, products of valuation rings, and the identification of étale cohomology and of cohomology with supports with those of the tilt.

Targets:

- Matched punctured opens of a henselian perfectoid pair and its tilt (`matched-punctured-opens`): Let p be a prime, A a ring and ϖ ∈ A with ϖ^p | p such that A is ϖ-henselian with bounded ϖ^∞-torsion and its ϖ-adic completion Â is (integral) perfectoid. Put A^♭ = lim_{a ↦ a^p} A/ϖA (the tilt of Â) and choose ϖ^♭ ∈ A^♭ with (ϖ^♭)^♯ a unit multiple of ϖ. The isomorphism A^♭/ϖ^♭ ≅ Â/ϖ = A/ϖ (the unpowered consequence of CS24 (2.1.2.2)–(2.1.2.3)) identifies Spec(A/ϖ) with Spec(A^♭/ϖ^♭). A matched pair of punctured opens is a pair (U, U^♭) of opens Spec A[1/ϖ] ⊆ U ⊆ Spec A and Spec A^♭[1/ϖ^♭] ⊆ U^♭ ⊆ Spec A^♭ whose closed complements, subsets of V(ϖ) and V(ϖ^♭), correspond under this identification. U ↦ U^♭ is an order isomorphism between the two sets of such opens.
- Multiplicative tilting of the generic fibre (`punctured-multiplicative-tilt`): Let A be perfectoid and ϖ-adically complete for ϖ ∈ A with ϖ^p | p, and ϖ^♭ ∈ A^♭ with (ϖ^♭)^♯ a unit multiple of ϖ. The p-power inverse limits satisfy compatible multiplicative bijections lim_{a↦a^p}(A[1/ϖ]) ≅ A^♭[1/ϖ^♭] and lim_{a↦a^p} A ≅ A^♭, the second being the multiplicative description of the tilt.
- Tilting of idempotents on punctured opens (`tilting-idempotents`): In the setting of EQ.8/matched-punctured-opens, for every matched pair (U, U^♭) there is a bijection Idem(U) ≅ Idem(U^♭) between the idempotents of Γ(U, O) and of Γ(U^♭, O), compatible with orthogonality and functorial in A and U.
- Étale cohomology of products of valuation rings and their tilts (`valuation-product-tilting`): Let A = ∏_{i∈I} V_i with each V_i a ϖ-adically complete valuation ring of rank ≤ 1 with algebraically closed fraction field, over a perfectoid base as in EQ.8/matched-punctured-opens. Then A is perfectoid with A^♭ = ∏ V_i^♭; for every quasi-compact open U ⊆ Spec A (resp. U^♭ ⊆ Spec A^♭) there are no nonsplit étale covers; RΓ_ét(U, G) and RΓ_ét(U^♭, G) are concentrated in degree 0, given by locally constant G-valued functions; and for matched (U, U^♭) they are identified functorially through EQ.8/tilting-idempotents.
- Algebraic tilting of étale cohomology (`tilting-etale-cohomology`): In the setting of EQ.8/matched-punctured-opens, for every matched pair (U, U^♭) and every torsion abelian group G there is an isomorphism RΓ_ét(U, G) ≅ RΓ_ét(U^♭, G), functorial in A, U and G.
- Tilting of cohomology with supports (`tilting-supports`): In the setting of EQ.8/matched-punctured-opens, for every closed Z ⊆ Spec(A/ϖA) and every torsion abelian group G, RΓ_Z(A, G) ≅ RΓ_{Z^♭}(A^♭, G), where Z^♭ ⊆ Spec(A^♭/ϖ^♭) corresponds to Z.
